objectives: Find the head of a subject phrase.
Match present-tense verbs to singular and plural subjects.

blocks.text: Subject–verb agreement means that the verb form matches the grammatical subject. This is especially visible in simple-present verbs and in forms of be. A singular third-person subject takes reads; a plural subject takes read.
blocks.idText: Kesesuaian subjek dan kata kerja ditentukan oleh inti subjek, bukan kata benda yang paling dekat dengan kata kerja.

blocks.text: Find the head noun or pronoun. Ignore phrases that describe it when choosing agreement.
The student with two dictionaries is prepared. The students with one dictionary are prepared.
blocks.note: Student and students are the heads; dictionaries and dictionary are not the subjects.

rows: Two separate people form a plural subject.
Be agrees with the following noun phrase.

blocks.incorrect: The list of reading tasks are long.
blocks.correct: The list of reading tasks is long.
blocks.explanation: List is the singular head. Tasks is part of an of-phrase.

blocks.incorrect: Each of the answers seem possible.
blocks.correct: Each of the answers seems possible.
blocks.explanation: Each is singular, so use seems in the simple present.

blocks.text: Most ordinary main verbs have the same form for singular and plural subjects in the simple past: she walked; they walked. Be is different: she was; they were. For this lesson, focus on clear count nouns and pronouns; collective nouns can involve additional choices depending on variety and meaning.

practice.prompt: The pages in this notebook ___ blank.
practice.explanation: Pages is the plural subject; in this notebook only describes the pages.

practice.prompt: Every learner ___ a different starting point.
practice.explanation: Every learner is singular, so use has.
